newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel attacks Europe's Security Council move.
newsitem.headline: Israel attacks Europe's Security Council move.

text.p: Israel on Saturday criticised European states which drafted a Security Council resolution, vetoed by the United States, calling on Israel to abandon plans to build a Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.
A senior adviser to Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, Freddy Eytan, called the resolution "one-sided" and welcomed the U.S. veto late on Friday.
The vote was 14 in favour, with only the U.S. against. As one of the council's five permanent members, its vote killed the resolution, drafted by Britain, France, Portugal and Sweden.
"We view gravely the European initiative which is unbalanced and one-sided and contrary to the position of the other members of the Security Council," Eytan told Reuters.

"Of course this again raises the issue of Europe's mediation in the peace process. We don't want every problem that arises to be taken to the Security Council rather they should be resolved by the sides.
"We were satisfied by the United States veto," Eytan said."

The veto followed a council debate in which virtually all of the nearly 50 speakers condemned Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews at a site called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
Israel regards the entire city of Jerusalem as its undivided capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

U.S. ambassador Bill Richardson criticised the Israeli action, both during the debate and after casting his veto, saying it undermined trust and confidence so badly needed in the Middle East peace process.
But he said the council was ... "not an appropriate forum for debating the issues now under negotiation between the parties."

The Palestine Liberation Organisation's United Nations observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, speaking after the veto, said: "In view of the failure of the council to fulfil its obligations, we would request from the members of the United Nations to agree to a meeting of the General Assembly in an emergency session."
There is no veto in the 185-member Assembly, whose decisions are not binding.
